paper_metadata.title: Nanoparticle-strengthened Ni2CoCrNb0.2 medium-entropy alloy with an ultrastrong cryogenic yield strength fabricated by additive manufacturing

evidence.quote: a Ni 2 CoCrNb 0.2 medium-entropy alloy (MEA) with D0 22 superlattice (noted as the γ′ ′ phase) is designed.
In this work, a novel γ′ ′ phase precipitation-hardened Ni 2 CoCrNb 0.2 MEA is designed by combining CALPHAD technology with the OVEC strategy.

The dark field (DF) image of the Ni 2 CoCrNb 0.2 MEA aged at 650 °C for 120 h is shown in Fig. 6 (a), indicating that disk-shaped precipitates with different crystal orientations were uniformly distributed in the matrix. According to statistics on the DF images, the proportion of disk-shaped precipitate in the matrix was 16%, which is agreement with the above CALPHAD results. The length and width of the disk-shaped precipitate were 10 nm and 3 nm, respectively.

Fig. 4 (a 1 ) shows that the microstructure of the Ni 2 CoCrNb 0.2 MEA was mainly composed of columnar crystals, and the growth direction was along the (100) direction [35] , as shown in Fig. 4 (a 2 ). Fig. 3 (a 3 ) shows the grain size distribution, and the statistical average grain size was 44.99 μm.

However, from the as-deposited state to the solid-solution state, the columnar crystal was transformed into an equiaxed crystal, the crystal had no obvious preferential orientation, and the average grain size grew to 87.38 μm, as shown in Fig. 4 (b 1 -b 3 ).

The nanoscale γ′ ′ phase precipitated. The tensile results indicated that the MEA had superior yield strengths of ∼1180 MPa and ∼1320 MPa and tensile strengths of ∼1335 MPa and ∼1552 MPa at 293 K and 77 K, respectively.
The γ′ ′ phase precipitation strengthening is the main strengthening mechanism, and its contribution to the yield strength is 741 MPa.

The mechanical properties of the Ni 2 CoCrNb 0.2 MEA demonstrated a strong temperature dependence, and the increased yield strength was mainly attributed to the increase in lattice friction stress at low temperatures.
